item.title: Anima Mundi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Metaphysical

Page Layout: Classic SCP, with Addenda including experiments and possibly recovery log

Elevator Pitch: Euclid object (which object, in particular, is to be decided), that imbues inanimate matter with consciousness, which is proven through a fictional (albeit grounded in real-life philosophy of mind) test - akin to the Turing test in Artificial Consciousness. Researchers try to figure out the extent to which the SCP affects objects, whether there are limitations to its effect, and whether the type of consciousness varies.

Central Narrative: The core of the idea is the test that determines consciousness in previously inanimate matter, and how researchers use it to determine the extent of the effect of this SCP. This will be fleshed out through experiment logs, trying out different types of objects or matter (say, for example, does it affect gases? if it does, does the air around it become conscious? Is there a limit to the size of the object? What do the objects feel? Does what they feel change depending on the type of object? etc.). The logs will build up to increasingly unsettling discoveries on inanimate objects.

+ show block
– hide block

An interesting piece will occur when researchers put the SCP in contact with living organisms. Plants wilt, and animals die. At first, researchers believe that this is because the SCP has an inverse effect on conscious organisms. However, after using it on a D-Class, they discover that the SCP grants consciousness to every single cell in their body, causing an immeasurable pain at the psychospace-metaphysical level, which in turn causes the D-Class to die in a horrible way.

Regarding Containment Procedures, this is Euclid because it could potentially make the very matter that contains it (walls, et al) conscious, as evidenced in a log with a near-containment breach, or the recovery log itself.

Another important theme of the SCP will be to explore the ethical implications of consciousness in inanimate objects - maybe with an Addendum including the Ethics Committee.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea can be very versatile in the experiment logs, with creative effects and results. The twist with already conscious organisms is also quite interesting.

Additional notes: Long time lurker, first-time poster - be gentle :). Also, I seem to recall an SCP with vaguely similar characteristics to this one, but couldn't find anything. Please do tell me if this is the case.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn
